subject: Vendor parity request from PixelFoundry — unpacking bundled credits vs usage discounts
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@pixelfoundry.io>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-12T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Exploring price parity option with bundled credits

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Samir and I walked through the latency profiles and the monitoring hooks and we like what Redwood brings. We have an incumbent offer on the table that is materially lower on unit price, but it bundles a large amount of prepaid compute credits (12 months) plus tooling only accessible if we commit to a specific GPU tier.

Before we take this to procurement, can you help us understand two things:
- Could Redwood match the effective blended unit economics they quoted, assuming we move to a 9–12 month committed path?
- If we can’t match outright, what packaging options (e.g., upfront migration credit + staged seat discount + usage floor) would keep the total TCO within 10% of their offer while preserving the flexibility we need?

Attached is the PDF of the incumbent offer redacted for pricing and the usage profile we expect for Q4+Q1. Happy to jump on a quick call.

Thanks,
Elena Ruiz
Head of Platform
PixelFoundry

Attachment: PF_offer-sep2026.pdf (PDF, 12 pages)

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Fwd: Exploring price parity option with bundled credits

Team — forwarding PixelFoundry's ask. Key constraints: they want parity within ~10% of incumbent blended cost and retain deployment flexibility (no hard GPU-tier lock).

Ask list:
- Ben: can you model a counter that mixes a migration credit (one-time), a 9-month committed usage tier, and a staged per-token discount? Please include an option with reserved capacity + burstable credits vs pure usage credits.
- Priya: procurement will likely push for vendor lock clauses on any big credit. What legal guardrails do we need so we don't create unilateral escape liabilities?
- Dylan: any operational caveats on offering a large upfront credit to a mid-market customer? Onboarding cost estimates, ramp timelines.

Goal: deliver a written counter and a simple comparison sheet we can send back by EOD Sep 14.

Marissa
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

Marissa / team — ran the numbers against their redacted sheet. High-level findings below, attachment is the comparison workbook.

Summary:
- The incumbent's unit price is ~25% lower on paper, but 70% of the value is buried in prepaid credits that expire at 12 months and require a strict GPU tier. That creates both utilization risk and lock-in.
- If PixelFoundry's profile follows the attachment forecast, we can offer a 9-month committed plan + $75k migration credit + staged discounts that hits within 8–9% of their blended TCO (option A).
- Option B (less aggressive) is a 6-month commit + $40k credit + per-token discount ramp that stays within ~12% of incumbent but preserves more flexibility and avoids reserved capacity SLAs.

Recommended commercial package (Option A — attach: rdw_counter_v2.pdf):
- 9-month commit at volume tier X (billing anchor)
- $75,000 migration credit applied over the first 3 invoices (credit line item)
- Staged per-token discounts: 10% months 1–3, 15% months 4–6, 20% months 7–9
- Optional reserved capacity add-on for month 3 onwards (customer opt-in) with a negotiated prepay that converts unused credits to term credits rather than cash refunds
- Onboarding SOW estimated at 4 weeks (Dylan to confirm), we would include 1 week free of prioritized migration support

Risks and operational notes:
- If they underconsume and leave unused prepaid credits, Redwood's exposure is the migration credit and reserved capacity bookkeeping — Priya, we should cap migration credit payout on milestones to reduce risk.
- Need legal language for convertibility of unused reserved credits and for termination assistance.

I attached: pricing-comparison-sheet.xlsx and rdw_counter_v2.pdf (redwood counter).

Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: rdw_counter_v2.pdf (PDF, 4 pages); pricing-comparison-sheet.xlsx (Excel)

From: priya_natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_coole@redwood.com>, dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-14T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Exploring price parity option with bundled credits

Thanks Ben — solid start. A few legal/procurement guardrails to surface before we send to the customer: 

- Milestone-based credit delivery: we should tie the $75k migration credit to three milestones (kickoff, successful model load & smoke test, post-cutover performance acceptance). This reduces straight cash exposure.
- Credit conversion clause: if reserved capacity is purchased and not consumed, allow conversion of remaining credits to 6-month term credits that apply to future invoices rather than refunds. Avoids cash refunds.
- Early termination language: define pro-rata true-up for credits and any prepaid bundles. Recommend a 60-day notice with a reconciliation period.
- Auditability: require mutually agreed consumption reporting (CSV export + API report) to reconcile credits monthly.

Please add these items to the counter doc. Also, we should not commit to a GPU-tier restriction in the main SOW; instead offer a recommended tier with ability to upgrade/downgrade with 14-day notice.

Priya Natarajan
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Marissa / Ben / Priya — thanks for the quick turnaround and the clear options. We reviewed Option A with the exec team and like the idea of tying migration credit to milestones and preserving convertibility of unused credits. Two quick asks before we move forward: 

1) Can you create a 1-page cost-vs-flexibility matrix we can share with procurement comparing: incumbent (prepaid + GPU lock), Redwood Option A (9m commit + migration credit + staged discounts + convertibility), Redwood Option B (6m commit + smaller credit)? That visual will speed approvals.

2) If we sign Option A, can we get a 30-day pilot waiver on the reserved capacity add-on so we can validate burst behavior without converting credits immediately?

If you can send the matrix and a slightly updated counter with Priya's milestone language, I believe procurement will greenlight. We aim to get this to legal by Sep 18.

Best,
Elena Ruiz
Head of Platform, PixelFoundry
